items.title: Anthropic Sells $81.3 Billion in Shares for a Record IPO
items.summary: Anthropic sold $81.3 billion in shares, valuing the company, which makes the Claude chatbot, at more than $1.5 trillion. It is the largest IPO on record, with shares beginning to trade on Nasdaq on Thursday.
items.why_it_matters: It is the biggest public offering ever and a landmark test of how much investors will pay for a frontier AI lab.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Neon, a new model in its Gemini 4 family, announced directly on the DeepMind blog.
items.why_it_matters: A new entry in Google's flagship model lineup keeps up the pace of frontier-model releases this week.

items.title: Genie 4 is now available
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced that Genie 4, the newest version of its Genie model, is now available.
items.why_it_matters: It's a new release in DeepMind's Genie line, one of the lab's ongoing frontier research efforts.

items.title: [AINews] GPT-6.2 Astra, the #2 Frontier Model is better and 20%-600% cheaper, but has mixed reviews; 6.2 Sol likely main workhorse
items.summary: OpenAI's new GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models lower benchmark costs by 20% to 600% versus the prior generation, with Astra ranked as the #2 frontier model. Early testers gave mixed reviews on what Astra is like to work with, and Sol is expected to become the main workhorse model.
items.why_it_matters: A steep price cut on a top-ranked frontier model changes the cost calculus for builders choosing which LLM to use.

items.title: Gemini on Mac can now use your computer
items.summary: Google's Gemini app for macOS now has a computer-use feature, letting it complete multi-step tasks across local files, desktop apps, and the web. Google suggests use cases like speeding up workflows, filling in forms, making presentations, and listing items for sale.
items.why_it_matters: It brings agentic computer control to the Mac, pushing Google ahead of Apple's own assistant on a key agent capability.

items.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
items.summary: Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform tasks such as browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services, according to a job listing seeking an engineer to lead the effort.
items.why_it_matters: It signals Apple is finally moving to field an agentic assistant to compete with Google, Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI's agents.

items.title: Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
items.summary: Google is updating its homepage to surface AI chats directly, with a collapsible sidebar that lets users open and continue AI conversations from the search homepage.
items.why_it_matters: Putting AI chat front and center on Google's homepage accelerates the shift of search traffic toward AI-first interfaces.

items.title: Meta's AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data, report says
items.summary: Meta employees reported that the Muse AI agent surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that didn't belong to them.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete example of an AI agent leaking or cross-contaminating private user data, a core safety risk for agentic products.

items.title: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency
items.summary: RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B, a 27-billion-parameter model it describes as pushing the frontier of post-training efficiency.
items.why_it_matters: Efficiency gains in post-training make it cheaper for smaller labs to produce competitive open models.

items.title: Claude solves two open problems in the physics of black holes
items.summary: Anthropic published research describing how its Claude model helped solve two previously open problems in black hole physics. The post drew heavy attention on Hacker News, reaching 398 points and 182 comments.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete example of a frontier LLM contributing to unresolved problems in theoretical physics, not just summarizing known work.

items.title: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
items.summary: The Commerce Department approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, according to Rep. Mast, even as members of Congress push for tighter export controls on chip sales to China in the wake of the Jensen Huang scandal.
items.why_it_matters: It's a major, specific data point on how much AI compute is still flowing to China despite export-control pressure.

items.title: California Attorney General Issues Investigative Subpoena to Nvidia
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia, opening a probe into whether the chipmaker misled investors.
items.why_it_matters: A state AG investigation adds legal risk for Nvidia on top of the China-related scrutiny already surrounding the company.

items.title: Artex Is Criminals' New Favorite 'Point-and-Shoot' AI Hacking Tool
items.summary: Artex and similar AI-powered penetration-testing tools let novice hackers scan targeted systems for vulnerabilities and successfully carry out attacks simply by feeding prompts to chatbots.
items.why_it_matters: It lowers the skill barrier for cyberattacks, a concrete example of AI tools being repurposed for offense faster than defenses adapt.

items.title: Datacentres to create 70% more carbon emissions by 2030, IEA report warns
items.summary: The IEA forecasts that the world's datacentres will produce 70% more carbon emissions within four years and will consume twice as much electricity by 2030 compared with today, with AI's global expansion driving three-quarters of that growth as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to meet demand.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete projection of how much AI's compute buildout will strain power grids and climate goals by 2030.

items.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: 385x more efficient inference
items.summary: A project called Energy-Based Reasoners claims an inference method up to 385 times more efficient than standard approaches. The post gained significant traction on Hacker News, with 273 points and 44 comments.
items.why_it_matters: A claimed order-of-magnitude efficiency gain in inference, if it holds up, could meaningfully cut the cost of running reasoning models.
